scope: Data SD2, Data OD, and the Divinity Strings Sound field
conclusion: Data SD2 and Data OD are byte-owned text tables. No Realmz runtime source path proves a central per-string sound field. Sounds are carried by caller records that reference messages, not by message records themselves.

dataFamilies.runtimeRole: Optional two-choice prompt label table preferred by question2 for negative/option indexes.
Divinity exposes a Strings screen sound box, but Realmz runtime sound behavior is stored on caller records rather than central string records.
notes: Text display plays generic sound 5000 when appropriate.
Action, battle, encounter, random-area, and thief records carry sound IDs beside message IDs where runtime behavior requires sound.
Opcode 19 Display Random String ignores EDCD sound-like slots in Realmz source even though Divinity guide text mentions optional sound for some string-related actions.
Providence should keep sound editing on the caller/action record that actually owns the sound byte.

providencePolicy: Do not add a per-string Sound field to the default Strings editor.
Expose sound fields only on source-backed caller records that actually play sounds.
Keep the Divinity Strings Sound UI as an unresolved binary/fixture target, not a scenario byte family.
